svg.text: Counting protected areas and measuring them are different questions
Each bubble is one of 196 territories: how many sites it lists, against how much of the planet they cover.
Both axes are logarithmic; the spread is five orders of magnitude. A departure counted as one site in 312,943 says nothing, and the
same departure measured in km² is the finding. Blue labels are the ten largest by area. Orange is the three territories with the most
sites per square kilometre — large records, small estates. Joint designations and the high seas are excluded.
Sweden lists 32,959 sites covering 264,641 km². The Cook Islands lists 3, covering 2,278,077 km².
By count Sweden is 10,986× the larger record. By area the Cook Islands is 9× the larger loss. Only one of those numbers is a fact about protection.
